text:
jordan: Heads-up — saw a tail p99 spike during last capacity burst (~09:42 UTC). Throughput steady but p99 jumped from ~210ms -> ~1.8s for about 2 minutes. Looks correlated with nodes joining and a flurry of kernel fallbacks. Quick notes below.

maya: What model + seq lengths? Any profiler traces?

chen: Model: gpt-compat-small:v2, mostly seq≈1024. Microbatching is dynamic (max_batch=16, target_latency=250ms). Attached profiler excerpt shows lots of kernel_select fallback events and KV cache misses right after scale-up. Paste of relevant logs: 

```
[09:42:11] worker-7 kernel_select: chosen=fast_rotary, fallback=attn_generic (reason=kernel_not_ready)
[09:42:12] worker-7 kv_cache: miss session=abc123, load_time=45ms
[09:42:12] worker-8 compile: nvptx_kernel compile_time=180ms (first-use)
[09:42:13] batcher: created microbatch size=1 for burst request id=xyz
[09:42:13] router: route_delay=12ms, enqueue_time=3ms
```

tess: KV cold-miss spike lines up with new workers not having warmed caches and kernel JIT/compiles. Also saw lots of tiny microbatches (size=1) — that increases per-token overhead.

samir: Hypothesis: autoscaler spins up nodes, they register quickly but the kernel selection & compilation + KV prefix cache populate lag. First few RPCs suffer compilation+kv loads. Two levers: reduce cold cost (precompile/warm kernels + preload KV) or avoid sending customer traffic to nodes until warm.

jordan: Right — tradeoff between SLOs: we tightened p95 target historically which pushed batcher to smaller microbatches and lower queueing latency, but during bursts p99 explodes due to cold-start penalties. We need heuristics that adapt microbatching and routing when scale-up events detected.

maya: Proposal list: 
1) pre-warm new instances with synthetic warmup requests (weights + KV prefetch) as part of scale-up.
2) keep a small min_replicas pool for bursty customers to avoid cold starts.
3) kernel_selector: bias towards a 'stable' kernel set on new nodes to avoid compile thrash.
4) transiently increase batching window (e.g., +100ms) for nodes in grace-period to increase microbatch sizes and amortize compile overhead.

chen: Ran a small staging experiment: added 150ms artificial batching delay for nodes during first 60s after join and kicked off a warmup script that preloaded top-10 KV keys. Result: baseline p99≈1.8s -> experiment p99≈420ms. p95 moved from 210ms -> 260ms. Throughput unchanged. Logs: "warmup: preloaded 10 keys in 120ms; kernel precompile time avg 90ms"

tess: Nice. That shows a clear tradeoff: small p95 regressions for large p99 improvement during bursts. :thumbsup: We need to decide SLO slack we can allocate.

samir: Ops ask: add per-node metrics: kernel_fallback_rate, kv_miss_ratio, first_5m_compile_time. Alert if kernel_fallback_rate > 2% over 5m. Also instrument scale-up windows so we can correlate.

jordan: I'll draft a runbook and PR: scaleup_warmup flag + default 60s grace period where we prefer batching and warm kernels. Also add an option to 'drain-unwarmed' so router avoids sending customer traffic to nodes until warm.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary created for scaleup-warmup in staging — https://ci.redwood/internal/5678 (runs 1000 synthetic bursts).

maya: Next steps: 1) prod-safe experiment with min_replicas=1 for a small subset of bursty customers, 2) add kernel_fallback_rate metric + dashboard, 3) run 2-week canary with warmup enabled. Who wants to own the dashboard?

samir: I'll own the dashboard. I'll also add alerts to SRE playbook.

jordan: Thanks all — I'll open the PR & link the runbook. If we can keep p95 regressions under ~20% while cutting p99 in half during bursts, that's a win.

deploy-bot: oncall-bot: noted. Tagging product for stake: @maya @jordan
